### 1 — Scene
A mixed buffet-style plate: a bone-in meat portion, two small orange-topped pastries, tofu, a fresh spring roll, and two pieces of tuna nigiri. The pastries and meat type are somewhat uncertain.

### 2 — Vessel
Likely a **26 cm dinner plate**.  
Area = 3.14 × 13² = **531 cm²**.

### 3 — Items
- Cooked meat on a large bone, possibly lamb
- Two small egg tarts or similar egg-filled pastries
- Several slices of cooked tofu
- One fresh vegetable spring-roll piece
- Two tuna nigiri

No separate sauce or added oil is clearly visible. The exposed bone is excluded from edible weight.

### 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy
Areas refer to the visible food footprints without double-counting overlaps. Energy densities include the food’s likely preparation.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Density | Estimated grams | kcal/100 g | kcal |

| Cooked meat, excluding bone | 15% | 80 cm² × 1.8 cm = 144 ml | 0.95 | 137 | 240 | 329 |
| Two small egg tarts | 14% | 74 cm² × 2 cm = 148 ml | 0.90 | 133 | 280 | 372 |
| Cooked tofu slices | 10% | 53 cm² × 2.8 cm = 148 ml | 0.95 | 141 | 140 | 197 |
| Fresh vegetable spring roll | 7% | 37 cm² × 2 cm = 74 ml | 0.65 | 48 | 100 | 48 |
| Two tuna nigiri | 10% | 53 cm² × 1.7 cm = 90 ml | 0.95 | 86 | 150 | 129 |

### 8 — Sanity check
The estimated edible coverage is **56%**, with additional space occupied by exposed bone. Several foods are thick or stacked, making **about 545 g and 1,075 kcal** plausible. The largest uncertainty is whether the orange rounds are egg tarts; a vegetable-based item would substantially lower the energy estimate.
